title: Adaptive Mosaic Kernel Prober — arch & seqlen-aware selector
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: our current kernel selection heuristics assume fairly stable sequence length distributions or rely on coarse arch buckets. In practice we serve heterogeneous fleets (A100/V100/H100) and mixed workloads where short-prefill + long-decode or vice-versa are common (chat + system prompts). Static heuristics lead to suboptimal kernel picks at the stage boundary (prefill vs decode) and higher p95 latency in tail cases.

Goal: deliver a lightweight, online probing and model fingerprinting system ("mosaic prober") that produces per-connection/per-model kernel recommendations that are both architecture-aware and sequence-length aware. The prober should: 1) execute microbenchmarks in a bounded budget during warm-up, 2) maintain per-(model,arch,seqlen-range) rolling profiles, 3) feed recommendations into the prefill/decode scheduler to pick kernels and operator tilings, and 4) expose diagnostics and rollback paths for safety.
tasks: Design probe specification: set of microbench ops (attention variants, matmul tilings, kvcache prefills) and budget/timeout
Implement probe harness in runtime with non-blocking background probe slots (prefill-window hook)
Add per-(model,arch,seqlen) fingerprint store with exponential smoothing and TTL
Integrate recommendations into prefill/decode scheduler: per-request kernel override with safety gate
Add regret-tracking metrics and automatic fallback if latency/regression observed
Instrument Console: per-model mosaic profile dashboard and probe health chart
Run staged experiments: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full with rollback playbook
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end probe runs in <250ms of controlled background CPU/GPU time for warmup on typical instance types
For short decode-heavy workloads (seq<=32) p50 decode latency decreases >=6% and p95 decreases >=4% on A100/H100 compared to baseline
No customer-visible increase in error rates or tokenization regressions during canary
Console shows per-model profile and probe success rate; alerts fire if probe failure rate >2% for 1h
Rollback path validated in staging and documented in runbook
updates: 2026-02-15: Spike completed — microbench candidate set defined (block-sparse attn, fused matmul+add, windowed KV prefetch). Notes uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Mosaic+Prober+Spike
2026-02-20: Initial probe harness prototype implemented. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4982 — basic non-blocking probe flow + fingerprint store

2026-02-24: Observed noisy samples on 8xV100 during small-batch probes due to thermal scaling and PCIe contention. Mitigation: add sample smoothing and randomized probe scheduling to avoid hot-spotting a device.
2026-03-01: Scheduler integration done for prefill path; decode hook still pending. Added safety gate that requires two successful probe sessions before overriding kernel selection for a model+arch.
2026-03-05: Canary rollout on staging (models: rw-7b-chat, rw-13b) for prefill path. Early telemetry: p50 prefill latency unchanged, p95 improved ~3% for mixed seqlen traces.
2026-03-08: Implemented regret tracker and automatic rollback when cumulative latency delta over 1h exceeds threshold. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5031

2026-03-10: Canary extended to decode path for rw-7b-chat on a subset of inbound traffic to test short-sequence decode optimization. Result: 6.8% p50 decode improvement and 4.1% p95 improvement on A100; no errors observed. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/runtime/perf?panel=mosaic-prober-canary
notes: Trade-offs: heavier initial probe budgets find better kernels but increase warm-up cost; we chose a conservative default (<=250ms) and allow tenant-configurable aggressiveness. We must balance probe sampling frequency to avoid amplifying GPU wear or contention on shared Dedicated nodes.
risks: Probe-induced noise causing regression on small instances or bursty workloads
Heat/thermal throttling biasing microbench results if not randomized
State explosion: large cardinality of (model,arch,seqlen) profiles could increase memory/metadata pressure
